captions.instagram:
How does a mosquito coil work?

A mosquito coil is a slow fuse wound into a spiral: nearly 70 cm of pressed powder that an ember crosses at 1.4 mm a minute, warming a few milligrams of insecticide into the air just ahead of itself. See why it is a spiral, what the vapour does to a mosquito's nerves, and why opening a window cuts the smoke and the protection by exactly the same share.

→ A mosquito coil comes as two spirals nested into one disc. Pull, and they snap apart.
→ It is sawdust or coconut-shell powder, a binder, dye, and a few milligrams of insecticide.
→ Why a spiral? It folds nearly 70 cm of slow fuse into a disc 12 cm wide.
→ The ember creeps 1.4 mm a minute, so one coil lasts about eight hours.
→ She tracks your breath from up to 50 metres, your shape from 15, your warmth in the last metre.

youtubeLong.title: How does a mosquito coil work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A mosquito coil is a slow fuse wound into a spiral: nearly 70 cm of pressed powder that an ember crosses at 1.4 mm a minute, warming a few milligrams of insecticide into the air just ahead of itself. See why it is a spiral, what the vapour does to a mosquito's nerves, and why opening a window cuts the smoke and the protection by exactly the same share.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/mosquitocoilclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/mosquitocoilclear

In this video:
• Two spirals, a stand and an ember. A coil comes as a flat disc that is really two spirals nested together; you snap them apart and stand one on a metal prong.
• A night-long fuse in a 12 cm disc. The length of a spiral is very nearly the area of its ring divided by the spacing of its turns: about 68 cm for a common coil.
• Gates held open. A mosquito finds you by the carbon dioxide in your breath from 10 to 50 metres, by your shape from 5 to 15 metres and by your warmth in the last metre.
• The window cuts both. A coil adds two things to a room: the vapour, and smoke.
• The same idea without the ember, and without the chemical. Liquid vaporisers and mats warm a similar active with a small electric heater, so there is no smoke from burning.
• Rules, care and resistance. In India a coil is an insecticide product under the Insecticides Act, 1968: it must be registered, and the pack must show the active, its strength and a registration number.
